value.zh: 元皇帝諱睿，字景文，宣帝曾孫，琅邪恭王覲之子也。
value.en: Emperor Yuan, whose personal name was Rui and courtesy name Jingwen, was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Jin and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.
value.literal: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.

value.zh: 咸寧二年生於洛陽，有神光之異，一室盡明，所藉槁如始刈。
value.en: He was born in Luoyang in 276, amid a strange glow that lit the whole chamber and left the bedding straw looking freshly mown.
value.literal: In the second year of Xianning he was born in Luoyang; there was a divine radiance anomaly; one room was entirely bright; the straw on which he lay was as if newly cut.

value.zh: 及長，白豪生於日角之左，隆準龍顏，目有精曜，顧眄煒如也。
value.en: As a man he bore a white filament beside the auspicious bump on his forehead, the high-bridged "dragon" profile of a ruler, and eyes so bright that every turn of his gaze seemed to flash with light.
value.literal: When grown, a white hair grew to the left of his sun-corner; high bridge nose and dragon countenance; his eyes had refined brilliance; his glances were radiant.

value.zh: 年十五，嗣位琅邪王。
value.en: At fifteen he inherited the title of Prince of Langye.
value.literal: At age fifteen he succeeded to the position of Prince of Langye.

value.zh: 幼有令問。
value.en: Even as a boy he was already known for an excellent name.
value.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.

value.zh: 及惠皇之際，王室多故，帝每恭儉退讓，以免於禍。
value.en: Under Emperor Hui, when the house of Jin was rocked by one crisis after another, he habitually kept to modesty, frugality, and deference so as to stay clear of disaster.
value.literal: When it came to the time of Emperor Hui, the royal house had many troubles; the emperor each time was respectful, frugal, yielding, in order to avoid calamity.

value.zh: 沈敏有度量，不顯灼然之迹，故時人未之識焉。
value.en: He was steady, astute, and large-minded, yet never advertised his abilities, so his contemporaries failed to see the ruler in him.
value.literal: Deep and keen, with capacity for tolerance, he did not display glaring traces; therefore people of the time did not recognize him.

value.zh: 惟侍中嵇紹異之，謂人曰：「琅邪王毛骨非常，殆非人臣之相也。」
value.en: Only Ji Shao, the palace attendant, saw something different in him and told others, "The Prince of Langye has a presence no ordinary man possesses; that is hardly the look of someone born to serve another."
value.literal: Only Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Shao thought him strange, saying to people: "The Prince of Langye's bearing is extraordinary; probably it is not the appearance of a subject."

value.zh: 三月，徵征西將軍戴若思、鎮北將軍劉隗還衛京都。
value.en: In the third month Dai Ruosi and Liu Wei were recalled from the front to defend the capital.
value.literal: In the third month he summoned General Who Conquers the West Dai Ruosi, General Who Guards the North Liu Wei to return and guard the capital region.

value.zh: 以司空王導爲前鋒大都督，以戴若思爲驃騎將軍，丹陽諸郡皆加軍號。
value.en: Wang Dao was named commander of the vanguard, Dai Ruosi became general of agile cavalry, and every Danyang county received a military designation.
value.literal: He appointed Minister of Works Wang Dao as Vanguard Grand Area Commander-in-Chief; appointed Dai Ruosi as General of Agile Cavalry; Danyang various commanderies all were added military titles.

value.zh: 加僕射周顗尚書左僕射，領軍王邃尚書右僕射。
value.en: Zhou Yi was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat and Wang Sui, the army commandant, to right vice director.
value.literal: He added Vice Director Zhou Yi as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Army Commandant Wang Sui as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 以太子右衛率周筵行冠軍將軍，統兵三千討沈充。
value.en: Zhou Yan, leader of the crown prince's right guard, was given the brevet rank of general who takes the championship and three thousand men to move against Shen Chong.
value.literal: He appointed the heir apparent's right guard leader Zhou Yan to act as General Who Takes the Championship, commanding three thousand troops to campaign against Shen Chong.

value.zh: 甲午，封皇子昱爲琅邪王。
value.en: On the jiawu day the emperor's son Sima Yu was invested as prince of Langye.
value.literal: On jiawu he enfeoffed the imperial son Yu as Prince of Langye.

value.zh: 劉隗軍于金城，右將軍周札守石頭，帝親被甲徇六師於郊外。
value.en: Liu Wei took position at Jincheng, Zhou Zha, general of the right, held Stone City, and the emperor buckled on his armor and rode through the six hosts outside the walls.
value.literal: Liu Wei encamped at Jincheng; General of the Right Zhou Zha guarded Stone Rampart; the emperor personally donned armor and inspected the six armies beyond the suburbs.

value.zh: 遣平南將軍陶侃領江州，安南將軍甘卓領荊州，各帥所統以躡敦後。
value.en: He ordered Tao Kan, the general who pacifies the south, to take charge of Jiangzhou and Gan Zhuo, the general who guards the south, of Jingzhou, each marching to fall on Wang Dun from behind.
value.literal: He dispatched General Who Pacifies the South Tao Kan to take Jiangzhou, General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo to take Jingzhou, each leading what they commanded to follow on Dun's rear.

value.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。
value.en: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.
value.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).

value.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。
value.en: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.
value.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.

value.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。
value.en: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.
value.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.

value.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。
value.en: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.
value.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.

value.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。
value.en: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.
value.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.

value.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。
value.en: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.
value.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.

value.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。
value.en: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
value.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.

value.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。」
value.en: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'
value.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.'

value.zh: 魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。
value.en: Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.
value.literal: Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'

value.zh: 寧康二年七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。
value.en: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month, Emperor Jianwen died just as the second mourning round collided with an intercalary month.
value.literal: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month Emperor Jianwen died—the second full mourning cycle met an intercalary month.

value.zh: 博士謝攸、孔粲議：「魯襄二十八年十二月乙未，楚子卒，實閏月而言十二月者，附正於前月也。
value.en: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.
value.literal: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.

value.zh: 喪事先遠，則應用博士吳商之言，以閏月祥。」
value.en: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."
value.literal: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."

value.zh: 尚書僕射謝安、中領軍王劭、散騎常侍鄭襲、右衛將軍殷康、驍騎將軍袁宏、散騎侍郎殷茂、中書郎車胤、左丞劉遵、吏部郎劉耽意皆同。
value.en: Xie An, Wang Shao, Zheng Xi, Yin Kang, Yuan Hong, Yin Mao, Che Yin, Liu Zun, and Liu Dan concurred.
value.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie An, Central Army commander Wang Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zheng Xi, General of the Right Guard Yin Kang, General of Swift Cavalry Yuan Hong, Cavalier Gentleman Yin Mao, Palace Secretariat Secretary Che Yin, Left Assistant Liu Zun, Personnel Section chief Liu Dan—all agreed.

value.zh: 康曰：「過七月而未及八月，豈可謂之逾期。
value.en: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?
value.literal: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?

value.zh: 必所不了，則當從其重者。」
value.en: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."
value.literal: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."

value.zh: 宏曰：「假值閏十二月而不取者，此則歲未終，固不可得矣。
value.en: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.
value.literal: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.

value.zh: 《漢書》以閏為後九月，明其同體也。」
value.en: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."
value.literal: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."

value.zh: 襲曰：「中宗、肅祖皆以閏月崩，祥除之變皆用閏之後月。
value.en: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.
value.literal: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.

value.zh: 先朝尚用閏之後月，今閏附七月，取之何疑，亦合遠日申情之言。
value.en: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.
value.literal: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.

value.zh: 又閏是後七而非八也，豈逾月之嫌乎！」
value.en: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"
value.literal: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"

value.zh: 尚書令王彪之、侍中王混、中丞譙王恬、右丞戴謐等議異，彪之曰：「吳商中才小官，非名賢碩儒、公輔重臣、為時所準則者。
value.en: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.
value.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.

value.zh: 又取閏無證據，直攬遠日之義，越祥忌，限外取，不合卜遠之理。
value.en: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.
value.literal: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.

value.zh: 又丞相桓公嘗論云，《禮》二十五月大祥。
value.en: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.
value.literal: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.

value.zh: 何緣越期取閏，乃二十六月乎？」
value.en: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"
value.literal: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"

value.zh: 於是啟曰：「或以閏附七月，宜用閏月除者。
value.en: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.
value.literal: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.

value.zh: 或以閏名雖除七月，而實以三旬別為一月，故應以七月除者。
value.en: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.
value.literal: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.

value.zh: 臣等與中軍將軍沖參詳，一代大禮，宜準經典。
value.en: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.
value.literal: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.

value.zh: 三年之喪，十三月而練，二十五月而畢，《禮》之明文也。
value.en: For the three-year mourning, the lian sacrifice is in the thirteenth month, and it is completed in the twenty-fifth month; this is the clear text of the rites.
value.literal: For the three-year mourning, the lian sacrifice is in the thirteenth month, and it is completed in the twenty-fifth month; this is the clear text of the rites.

value.zh: 《陽秋》之義，閏在年內，則略而不數。
value.en: According to the meaning of the Yangqiu, when an intercalary month is inside the year, it is omitted and not counted.
value.literal: According to the meaning of the Yangqiu, when an intercalary month is inside the year, it is omitted and not counted.

value.zh: 明閏在年外，則不應取之以越期忌之重，禮制祥除必正期月故也。」
value.en: It is clear that when the intercalary month is outside the year, one should not take it and thereby exceed the weight of the term and taboo, because the ritual system for xiang sacrifice and removal must correct the numbered months."
value.literal: It is clear that when the intercalary month is outside the year, one should not take it and thereby exceed the weight of the term and taboo, because the ritual system for xiang sacrifice and removal must correct the numbered months."

value.zh: 己酉晦，帝除縞即吉。
value.en: On jiyou, month-end, the sovereign left white mourning and resumed felicity garb.
value.literal: On jiyou, the last day of the month, the emperor shed mourning white silk and returned to auspicious dress.'

value.zh: 徐廣論曰：「凡辨義詳理，無顯據明文可以折中奪易，則非疑如何。
value.en: Xu Guang's discussion said, "In general, when distinguishing meaning and detailing principle, if there is no manifest evidence or clear text by which to decide and overturn the matter, then how can it not be doubtful?
value.literal: Xu Guang's discussion said, "In general, when distinguishing meaning and detailing principle, if there is no manifest evidence or clear text by which to decide and overturn the matter, then how can it not be doubtful?

value.zh: 禮疑從重，喪易甯戚，順情通物，固有成言矣。
value.en: When ritual is doubtful, one follows the weightier option; in mourning, when changing, one prefers grief. To follow feeling and comprehend things certainly already has established sayings.
value.literal: When ritual is doubtful, one follows the weightier option; in mourning, when changing, one prefers grief. To follow feeling and comprehend things certainly already has established sayings.

value.zh: 彪之不能徵援正義，有以相屈，但以名位格人，君子虛受，心無適莫，豈其然哉！
value.en: Biaozhi could not cite and invoke correct meaning in a way that would make others yield, but only used name and rank to restrain people. The gentleman receives emptily, and in his heart has no fixed leaning; how could this be so!
value.literal: Biaozhi could not cite and invoke correct meaning in a way that would make others yield, but only used name and rank to restrain people. The gentleman receives emptily, and in his heart has no fixed leaning; how could this be so!

value.zh: 執政從而行之，其殆過矣。」
value.en: Those who held government followed and carried it out; this was probably an error."
value.literal: Those who held government followed and carried it out; this was probably an error."

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充、尚書令諸葛恢、尚書謝廣、光祿勳留擢、丹楊尹殷融、護軍將軍馮懷、散騎常侍鄧逸等咸從潭議，由是太后配食武帝。
value.en: Yu Yi, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.
value.literal: Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.

value.zh: 安平獻王孚
value.en: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.
value.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).

value.zh: 初，騰發并州，次於真定。
value.en: Leaving Bing he paused at Zhending.
value.literal: At first when Teng set out from Bing Province he halted at Zhending.

value.zh: 值大雪，平地數尺，營門前方數丈雪融不積，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，表獻之。
value.en: Snow melted oddly at his gate; digging revealed a jade horse sent to court.
value.literal: It happened there was great snow several chi deep on level ground; before the camp gate several zhang of ground showed melted snow not accumulating; Teng wondered and dug obtaining a jade horse about a chi high which he memorialized and presented.

value.zh: 其後公師籓與平陽人汲桑等為群盜，起於清河鄃縣，眾千餘人，寇頓丘，以葬成都王穎為辭，載穎主而行，與張泓故將李豐等將攻鄴。
value.en: Ji Sang's gang marched under Ying's tablet to threaten Ye.
value.literal: Later duke-lord Shi Fan with Pingyang men Ji Sang and others formed bandit gangs rising in Shu county of Qinghe over one thousand strong raiding Dunqiu using burying Prince of Chengdu Ying as pretext loading Ying's spirit tablet marching with Zhang Hong's old general Li Feng intending to attack Ye.

value.zh: 騰曰：「孤在并州七年，胡圍城不能克。
value.en: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.
value.literal: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.

value.zh: 汲桑小賊，何足憂也。」
value.en: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'
value.literal: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'

value.zh: 及豐等至，騰不能守，率輕騎而走，為豐所害。
value.en: The raid overwhelmed him; fleeing lightly armed he fell to Feng.
value.literal: When Feng and others arrived Teng could not defend and led light horse fleeing and was killed by Feng.

value.zh: 四子：虞、矯、紹、確。
value.en: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
value.literal: Four sons: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.

value.zh: 虞有勇力，騰之被害，虞逐豐，豐投水而死。
value.en: Yu avenged his father driving Feng into the river.
value.literal: Yu had courage and strength; when Teng was harmed Yu pursued Feng who threw himself in water and died.

value.zh: 是日，虞及矯、紹並钜鹿太守崔曼、車騎長史羊恆、從事中郎蔡克等又為豐餘黨所害，及諸名家流移依鄴者，死亡並盡。
value.en: The bloodbath wiped Julu officials and refugee clans at Ye.
value.literal: That same day Yu together with Jiao and Shao and Julu governor Cui Man chariot-and-cavalry chief clerk Yang Heng consultant Cai Ke were again harmed by Feng's remaining faction and renowned families taking refuge at Ye perished altogether.

value.zh: 初，鄴中雖府庫虛竭，而騰資用甚饒。
value.en: Ye's arsenals stood empty yet Teng hoarded wealth.
value.literal: At first though Ye granaries were exhausted Teng's private wealth was very ample.

value.zh: 性儉嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米可數升，帛各丈尺，是以人不為用，遂致於禍。
value.en: His miserly handfuls of grain and cloth bought no loyalty and brought disaster.
value.literal: By nature stingy he showed no generosity; facing crisis he then gifted officers several sheng of rice and bolts only one zhang therefore men would not serve him and ruin followed.

value.zh: 及苟晞救鄴，桑還平陽。
value.en: Gou Xi's relief sent Ji Sang back toward Pingyang.
value.literal: When Gou Xi relieved Ye Sang returned to Pingyang.

value.zh: 于時盛夏，屍爛壞不可復識，騰及三子骸骨不獲。
value.en: It was midsummer, and the corpses had decayed beyond recognition; the remains of Teng and his three sons could not be recovered.
value.literal: It was then deep summer; corpses rotted beyond recognition and Teng's and his three sons' bones could not be recovered.

value.zh: 庶子確立。
value.en: His son by a secondary consort, Sima Que, succeeded him.
value.literal: His son by a secondary consort, Que, succeeded him.

value.zh: 敬王恬，字元愉，少拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、黃門郎、御史中丞。
value.en: Sima Tian rose through palace attendant posts to censor-in-chief.
value.literal: Prince Jing Tian courtesy Yuanyu youth appointed irregular cavalry gentleman progressively irregular cavalry attendant yellow-gate gentleman palace Assistant chief.

value.zh: 值海西廢，簡文帝登阼，未解嚴，大司馬桓溫屯中堂，吹警角，恬奏劾溫大不敬，請科罪。
value.en: Before demobilization Tian impeached Huan Wen's trumpet fanfare as lèse-majesté.
value.literal: When Haixi was deposed Emperor Jianwen ascended throne martial law not yet lifted Grand Marshal Huan Wen encamped Central Hall sounding alarm horns Tian memorialized impeaching Wen greatly irreverent requesting sentencing crime.

value.zh: 溫視奏歎曰：「此兒乃敢彈我，真可畏也。」
value.en: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'
value.literal: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。
value.en: Adult Yu spurned books, slighted tutors, and played with pages.
value.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

value.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」
value.en: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
value.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

value.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」
value.en: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
value.literal: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"

value.zh: 太子所幸蔣美人生男，又言宜隆其賞賜，多為皇孫造玩弄之器，太子從之。
value.en: When Consort Jiang bore a son they pushed costly toys and stipends—Yu complied.
value.literal: When Lady Jiang, whom the crown prince favored, bore a son, they also said rewards should be lavish and many toys fashioned for the imperial grandson; the crown prince obeyed.

value.zh: 於是慢弛益彰，或廢朝侍，恆在後園遊戲。
value.en: He skipped audiences for back-garden games.
value.literal: Thereupon his arrogance and laxness grew plainer; sometimes he skipped court attendance and constantly played in the rear garden.

value.zh: 愛埤車小馬，令左右馳騎，斷其鞅勒，使墮地為樂。
value.en: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.
value.literal: He loved low carts and ponies; he had attendants gallop them, then cut their harness straps and bridles to amuse himself by making them fall.

value.zh: 或有犯忤者，手自捶擊之。
value.en: He thrashed servants himself.
value.literal: If anyone offended him he personally beat them.

value.zh: 性拘小忌，不許繕壁修牆，正瓦動屋。
value.en: He banned builders from touching plaster or tiles—superstition.
value.literal: Given to petty taboos, he forbade plastering walls, repairing fences, or straightening roof-tiles.

value.zh: 而于宮中為市，使人屠酤，手揣斤兩，輕重不差。
value.en: Yet he set up a market inside the palace, had others butcher animals and sell wine, and judged weights with his own hands without error.
value.literal: Yet inside the palace he opened a market, had people butcher and sell ale, and weighed purchases in his own hands to the exact ounce.

value.zh: 其母本屠家女也，故太子好之。
value.en: His mother was originally a butcher’s daughter, which is why the crown prince enjoyed this.
value.literal: His mother had been a butcher's daughter; therefore the crown prince delighted in it.

value.zh: 又令西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，而收其利。
value.en: He peddled greens, dye seed, chicken, and flour from West Garden for cash.
value.literal: He also ordered the Western Garden to sell mallow, indigo seed, chickens, flour, and the like, pocketing the profit.

value.zh: 東宮舊制，月請錢五十萬，備於眾用，太子恆探取二月，以供嬖寵。
value.en: The Eastern Palace normally received five hundred thousand cash a month for all its expenses; he habitually drew two months in advance to provide for his favorites.
value.literal: Eastern Palace precedent allotted five hundred thousand cash monthly for general expenses; the crown prince habitually drew two months ahead to supply favorites.

value.zh: 洗馬江統陳五事以諫之，太子不納，語在《統傳》中。
value.en: Jiang Tong's five memorials went unheard—see his chapter.
value.literal: Groom of the Household Jiang Tong presented five admonitions; the crown prince rejected them—the account appears in Jiang Tong's biography.

value.zh: 舍人杜錫以太子非賈后所生，而後性凶暴，深以為憂，每盡忠規勸太子修德進善，遠於讒謗。
value.en: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.
value.literal: Gentleman-of-the-Household Du Xi, because the crown prince was not Empress Jia's son and the empress was savage by nature, deeply worried; he repeatedly urged the crown prince to cultivate virtue and do good, standing far from slander.

value.zh: 太子怒，使人以針著錫常所坐氈中而剌之。
value.en: Angered, Yu had someone put needles into the felt mat where Du Xi usually sat, so that they would prick him.
value.literal: The crown prince grew angry and had someone sew needles into Du Xi's usual felt mat to stab him.

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。
value.en: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.
value.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.

value.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。
value.en: Twelfth month Jia feigned imperial illness to lure Yu to court.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

value.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。
value.en: She hid him, fed him wine and dates through Chen Wu until he was drunk.
value.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

value.zh: 使黃門侍郎潘岳作書草，若禱神之文，有如太子素意，因醉而書之，令小婢承福以紙筆及書草使太子書之。
value.en: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the Crown Prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.
value.literal: She had Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pan Yue draft a prayer text mimicking the crown prince's usual intent; because he was drunk she made him copy it, having the young maid Chengfu bring paper, brush, and draft.

value.zh: 文曰：「陛下宜自了；
value.en: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;
value.literal: The text read: "Your Majesty should end your own life;

value.zh: 不自了，吾當入了之。
value.en: Or I will finish you.
value.literal: if you do not end it yourself, I shall come in and end it for you.

value.zh: 中宮又宜速自了；
value.en: The empress too should quickly end her own life;
value.literal: The empress too should quickly end her own life;

value.zh: 不了，吾當手了之。
value.en: Or I will kill her myself.
value.literal: if she does not, I shall end her life with my own hands.

value.zh: 並謝妃共要克期而兩發，勿疑猶豫，致後患。
value.en: Consort Xie and I strike together—no delay.
value.literal: Together with Consort Xie we agreed a joint date for simultaneous rising—do not hesitate and breed later trouble.

value.zh: 茹毛飲血於三辰之下，皇天許當掃除患害，立道文為王，蔣為內主。
value.en: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.
value.literal: We shall eat raw flesh and drink blood beneath the three luminaries; High Heaven grants us leave to sweep away the scourge, enthrone Daowen as king, and install Jiang as inner mistress.

value.zh: 願成，當三牲祠北君，大赦天下。
value.en: Then sacrifice to the Northern Lord and amnesty all.
value.literal: When wish is fulfilled we shall sacrifice three victims to the Northern Lord and proclaim an empire-wide amnesty.

value.zh: 要疏如律令。」
value.en: So commands the spell.'
value.literal: Let this sworn petition take effect as commanded.

value.zh: 太子醉迷不覺，遂依而寫之，其字半不成。
value.en: Too drunk and confused to realize what he was doing, the crown prince copied it, but half the characters were incomplete.
value.literal: The crown prince was too drunk and confused to notice; he copied accordingly; half the characters failed to form.

value.zh: 既而補成之，后以呈帝。
value.en: Helpers patched characters before Jia showed Hui.
value.literal: They afterward filled them in; the empress presented it to the emperor.

value.zh: 帝幸式乾殿，召公卿入，使黃門令董猛乙太子書及青紙詔曰：「遹書如此，今賜死。」
value.en: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: "Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death."
value.literal: The emperor visited Shi-Qian Hall, summoned dukes and ministers, and had Yellow Gate Chief Dong Meng display the crown prince's script with an edict on blue paper: 'Yu has written thus—now sentence him to death.'

value.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。
value.en: Silence fell until Zhang Hua and Pei Wei defended Yu.
value.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.

value.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」
value.en: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."
value.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'

value.zh: 議至日西不決。
value.en: Debate stalled till dusk.
value.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

value.zh: 後懼事變，乃表免太子為庶人，詔許之。
value.en: Jia feared delay—demoted Yu to commoner instead.
value.literal: The empress feared events might shift and therefore memorialized to degrade the crown prince to commoner status; an edict approved.

value.zh: 於是使尚書和郁持節，解結為副，及大將軍梁王肜、鎮東將軍淮南王允、前將軍東武公澹、趙王倫、太保何劭詣東宮，廢太子為庶人。
value.en: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.
value.literal: Thereupon Minister He Yu was dispatched with insignia, with Xie Jie as deputy, together with General-in-Chief Sima Rong, Prince of Liang; Eastern Garrison General Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan; Forward General Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu; Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao; and Grand Guardian He Shao. They went to the Eastern Palace to depose the crown prince as a commoner.

value.zh: 是日太子游玄圃，聞有使者至，改服出崇賢門，再拜受詔，步出承華門，乘粗犢車。
value.en: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.
value.literal: That day the crown prince roamed the Mystic Garden; hearing envoys arrived he changed clothes, exited Chongxian Gate, twice bowed receiving the edict, walked out Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart.

value.zh: 澹以兵仗送太子妃王氏、三皇孫于金墉城，考竟謝淑妃及太子保林蔣俊。
value.en: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.
value.literal: Dan escorted Crown Princess Wang and the three imperial grandsons to Jinyong under armed guard, and interrogated Consort Xie and the crown prince’s Lady Baolin Jiang Jun to death.

value.zh: 明年正月，賈后又使黃門自首，欲與太子為逆。
value.en: Next New Year Jia staged a Yellow Gate confession implicating Yu.
value.literal: The next first month Empress Jia again had a Yellow Gate confess plotting rebellion with the crown prince.

value.zh: 詔以黃門首辭班示公卿。
value.en: An edict circulated the Yellow Gate eunuch’s confession among the dukes and ministers.
value.literal: An edict circulated the confession among dukes and ministers.

value.zh: 又遣澹以千兵防送太子，更幽于許昌宮之別坊，令治書御史劉振持節守之。
value.en: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.
value.literal: She further sent Dan with a thousand troops to escort the crown prince, moving him to a separate compound of Xuchang palace under Supervising Secretary Liu Zhen with insignia.

value.zh: 先是，有童謠曰：「東宮馬子莫聾空，前至臘月纏汝閤。」
value.en: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: "Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber."
value.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme ran: 'Eastern Palace foals—don't plug your ears empty; come twelfth month they'll twine your chamber.'

value.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」
value.en: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
value.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

value.zh: 南風，后名；
value.en: South Wind' meant Empress Jia.
value.literal: South Wind' was the empress's name.

value.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。
value.en: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
value.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

value.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
value.en: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
value.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

value.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
value.en: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
value.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

value.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
value.en: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
value.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

value.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
value.en: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
value.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

value.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
value.en: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
value.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

value.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
value.en: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.
value.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

value.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。
value.en: His plea for son's title failed.
value.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.

value.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。
value.en: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
value.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.

value.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
value.en: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
value.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

value.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。
value.en: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
value.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

value.zh: '即便作表求入。
value.en: He requested audience.
value.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.

value.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
value.en: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
value.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

value.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
value.en: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
value.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

value.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
value.en: They parked him in an empty room.
value.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.

value.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
value.en: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
value.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

value.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
value.en: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
value.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

value.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
value.en: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
value.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.

value.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
value.en: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
value.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

value.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
value.en: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
value.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

value.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
value.en: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
value.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

value.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。
value.en: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
value.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.

value.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。
value.en: Empty stomach worried him.
value.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.

value.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
value.en: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.
value.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.

value.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
value.en: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
value.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!

value.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
value.en: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
value.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

value.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。
value.en: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
value.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

value.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。
value.en: Cornered he drank more.
value.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.

value.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。
value.en: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.
value.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.

value.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。
value.en: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."
value.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'

value.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。
value.en: He found white and green paper inside.
value.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.

value.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。
value.en: Runners said the emperor waited.
value.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'

value.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
value.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
value.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

value.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。
value.en: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
value.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.

value.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」
value.en: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
value.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

value.zh: 太子既廢非其罪，眾情憤怨。
value.en: Injustice against Yu enraged the capital.
value.literal: After the crown prince was deposed without crime, popular feeling seethed with anger.

value.zh: 右衛督司馬雅，宗室之疏屬也，與常從督許超並有寵于太子，二人深傷之，說趙王倫謀臣孫秀曰：「國無適嗣，社稷將危，大臣之禍必起。
value.en: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: "The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.
value.literal: Right Guard Commandant Sima Ya, a distant kinsman of the imperial house, and Attendant Commandant Xu Chao, both favorites of the crown prince, grieved deeply; they told Sun Xiu, stratagemist to Lun, Prince of Zhao: 'The state has no true heir—altar and grain will be imperiled; great ministers' disaster is sure to rise.

value.zh: 而公奉事中宮，與賈后親密，太子之廢，皆云豫知，一旦事起，禍必及矣。
value.en: "You serve the empress and are close to her. Everyone says you knew in advance of the prince’s deposition. If trouble breaks out, disaster will surely reach you too."
value.literal: You serve the inner palace in the empress's confidence; all say you foreknew the crown prince's deposition—should trouble erupt, disaster will reach you too.

value.zh: 何不先謀之！」
value.en: Why not plot first!"
value.literal: Why not plot first!'

value.zh: 秀言于趙王倫，倫深納焉。
value.en: Sun Xiu sold the plot to Sima Lun.
value.literal: Xiu reported to Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Lun accepted fully.

value.zh: 計既定，而秀說倫曰：「太子為人剛猛，若得志之日，必肆其情性矣。
value.en: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, "The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.
value.literal: With the plan set, Xiu said to Lun, 'The crown prince is by nature rigid and fierce; if he gains his will he will certainly give free rein to his temper.

value.zh: 明公素事賈后，街談巷議，皆以公為賈氏之黨。
value.en: Lun was branded Jia's man.
value.literal: You have long served Empress Jia; street talk names you a Jia partisan.

value.zh: 今雖欲建大功于太子，太子雖將含忍宿忿，必不能加賞於公，當謂公逼百姓之望，翻覆以免罪耳。
value.en: Yu would not thank Lun for a late defection.
value.literal: Now even if you wish to build great merit for the crown prince, though he may swallow old rage for a time he cannot reward you—he will think you only reversed under popular pressure to escape blame.

value.zh: 若有瑕釁，猶不免誅。
value.en: One slip and Lun's head would roll.
value.literal: If any flaw appears you will still not escape execution.

value.zh: 不若遷延卻期，賈后必害太子，然後廢賈后，為太子報仇，猶足以為功，乃可以得志。」
value.en: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will."
value.literal: Better delay: Empress Jia is sure to harm the crown prince; then depose Jia, avenge the crown prince—merit enough to win your will.'

value.zh: 倫然之。
value.en: Lun assented.
value.literal: Lun agreed.

value.zh: 秀因使反間，言殿中人欲廢賈后，迎太子。
value.en: Sun Xiu spread rumors of a palace plot to restore Yu.
value.literal: Xiu therefore launched counter-espionage, saying men of the palace meant to depose Empress Jia and welcome the crown prince.

value.zh: 賈后聞之憂怖，乃使太醫令程據合巴豆杏子丸。
value.en: Jia panicked and had Cheng Ju mix purgative poison.
value.literal: When the empress heard it she was terrified and ordered Court Physician-in-Chief Cheng Ju to compound croton and apricot-kernel pills.

value.zh: 三月，矯詔使黃門孫慮齋至許昌以害太子。
value.en: Third month a fake edict sent Sun Lü to kill Yu at Xuchang.
value.literal: In the third month a forged edict sent Yellow Gate Sun Lü to Xuchang to murder the crown prince.

value.zh: 初，太子恐見鴆，恆自煮食於前。
value.en: Yu had cooked for himself to avoid cup poison.
value.literal: Earlier the crown prince had feared being poisoned and always cooked his own food before him.

value.zh: 慮以告劉振，振乃徙太子于小坊中，絕不與食，宮中猶於牆壁上過食與太子。
value.en: Lü reported this to Liu Zhen, who moved the crown prince to a small compound and denied him food. Palace personnel still passed food to him over the walls.
value.literal: Lü reported to Liu Zhen; Zhen thereupon moved the crown prince to a small ward, cut off all food, yet the palace still passed food over the wall to the crown prince.

value.zh: 慮乃逼太子以藥，太子不肯服，因如廁，慮以藥杵椎殺之，太子大呼，聲聞於外。
value.en: Sun Lü beat Yu to death in the latrine with a pestle—screams escaped.
value.literal: Lü then forced medicine on the crown prince; the crown prince refused to swallow; while using the privy Lü killed him with a medicine pestle; the crown prince cried loudly—the sound carried outside.

value.zh: 時年二十三。
value.en: He died at twenty-three.
value.literal: He was twenty-three sui.

value.zh: 將以庶人禮葬之，賈后表曰：「遹不幸喪亡，傷其迷悖，又早短折，悲痛之懷，不能自己。
value.en: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: "Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.
value.literal: They proposed burying him by commoner rites; Empress Jia memorialized: 'Yu has unfortunately died—I mourn his confusion and error and early cutting-off; grief overwhelms me.

value.zh: 妾私心冀其刻肌刻骨，更思孝道，規為稽顙，正其名號。
value.en: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.
value.literal: I privately hoped he would take the lesson deeply to heart and reflect anew on filial duty; a plea in prostration was intended to restore his title.

value.zh: 此志不遂，重以酸恨。
value.en: She claimed thwarted maternal hopes.
value.literal: That aim failed—doubly bitter regret.

value.zh: 遹雖罪在莫大，猶王者子孫，便以匹庶送終，情實憐湣，特乞天恩，賜以王禮。
value.en: She asked royal burial despite his crimes.
value.literal: Though Yu's guilt was utmost he remains an imperial grandson—to dispatch him as a mere commoner truly pity—may Heaven grant kingly burial.

value.zh: 妾誠暗淺不識禮義，不勝至情，冒昧陳聞。」
value.en: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize."
value.literal: Your servant is dull and shallow, ignorant of ritual propriety, overwhelmed by utmost feeling—rashly venturing to memorialize.'

value.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。
value.en: The court buried him as Guangling prince.
value.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 臧字敬文。
value.en: Second son Zang, styled Jingwen.
value.literal: Zang, courtesy name Jingwen.

value.zh: 永康元年四月，封臨淮王。
value.en: Yongkang fourth month made Linhuai prince.
value.literal: In the fourth month of Yongkang year one he was enfeoffed Prince of Linhuai.

value.zh: 己巳，詔曰：「咎征數發，奸回作變，遹既逼廢，非命而沒。
value.en: On jisi day an edict stated: "Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.
value.literal: On jisi day an edict stated: 'Ill omens pile; crafty factions stir; Yu was driven from office and died unnaturally.

value.zh: 今立臧為皇太孫。
value.en: Zang named grand-heir.
value.literal: Now we establish Zang as imperial grandson-heir.

value.zh: 還妃王氏以母之，稱太孫太妃。
value.en: Let Consort Wang return to act as his mother, with the title Grand Consort Dowager of the Imperial Grandson-Heir.
value.literal: Consort Wang returns to mother him—styled Grand Heir Consort Dowager.

value.zh: 太子官屬即轉為太孫官屬。
value.en: Staff slid from heir to grand-heir titles.
value.literal: Eastern Palace staff transferred to grand-heir posts.

value.zh: 趙王倫行太孫太傅。」
value.en: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir."
value.literal: Lun, Prince of Zhao, acted Grand Tutor to the imperial grandson-heir.'

value.zh: 五月，倫與太孫俱之東宮，太孫自西掖門出，車服侍從皆湣懷之舊也。
value.en: May procession exited the west palace gate in Yu's old livery.
value.literal: In the fifth month Lun and the grand heir went together to the Eastern Palace; the grand heir exited the Western Side Gate—carriages, dress, and attendants all followed Minhuai's old train.

value.zh: 到銅駝街，宮人哭，侍從者皆哽咽，路人抆淚焉。
value.en: Luoyang wept along Bronze Camel Street.
value.literal: Reaching Bronze Camel Avenue palace women wept; attendants choked; passersby wiped tears.

value.zh: 桑復生於西廂，太孫廢，乃枯。
value.en: Omen mulberry mirrored heir's fall.
value.literal: The mulberry sprouted again west of the wing; when the grand heir was deposed it withered.

value.zh: 永甯元年正月，趙王倫篡位，廢為濮陽王，與帝俱遷金墉，尋被害。
value.en: Yongning coup demoted Zang—murdered at Jinyong.
value.literal: In the first month of Yongning year one Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and demoted Zang to Prince of Puyang. Zang moved with the emperor to Jinyong and was murdered soon afterward.

value.zh: 太安初，追諡曰哀。
value.en: Tai'an era canonized Ai.
value.literal: Early in Tai'an posthumous title Ai was granted.

value.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
value.en: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.
value.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.

value.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
