value.en: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
value.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

value.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
value.en: The realm expected greatness.
value.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

value.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。
value.en: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
value.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

value.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
value.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
value.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

value.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
value.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
value.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

value.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
value.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
value.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

value.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
value.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
value.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

value.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
value.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
value.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

value.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
value.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
value.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

value.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
value.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
value.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

value.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
value.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
value.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

value.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
value.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
value.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

value.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
value.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
value.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；
value.en: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.
value.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;

value.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。
value.en: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.
value.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.

value.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；
value.en: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;
value.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;

value.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。
value.en: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.
value.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.

value.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；
value.en: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;
value.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;

value.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。
value.en: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.
value.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.

value.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。
value.en: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.
value.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.

value.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。
value.en: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.
value.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?

value.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！
value.en: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.
value.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?

value.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。
value.en: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.
value.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.

value.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。
value.en: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.
value.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.

value.zh: 孟陋，字少孤，武昌人也。
value.en: Meng Lou, courtesy name Shaogu, came from Wuchang.
value.literal: Meng Lou, styled Shaogu, was a man of Wuchang.

value.zh: 吳司空宗之曾孫也。
value.en: He was great-grandson of Wu minister Meng Zong.
value.literal: He was great-grandson of Wu's minister of works Meng Zong.

value.zh: 兄嘉，桓溫征西長史。
value.en: His brother Meng Jia had been chief clerk under Huan Wen.
value.literal: His elder brother Meng Jia was chief clerk on Huan Wen's western campaign.

value.zh: 陋少而貞立，清操絕倫，布衣蔬食，以文籍自娛。
value.en: Young, he was chaste, austere, in sackcloth and gruel, happy only in books.
value.literal: Lou in youth was chaste and established, his pure conduct unmatched, in plain cloth and coarse food, taking pleasure in books.

value.zh: 口不及世事，未曾交遊，時或弋釣，孤興獨往，雖家人亦不知其所之也。
value.en: He never gossiped, rarely visited anyone, fished or hunted alone—his family never knew his path.
value.literal: His mouth did not touch the affairs of the age; he never socialized; sometimes he shot or fished, alone with his whim—even his household did not know where he went.

value.zh: 喪母，毀瘠殆於滅性，不飲酒食肉十有餘年。
value.en: His mother's death left him skeletal; he ate no meat over ten years.
value.literal: When his mother died, he wasted his flesh almost to extinguishing nature; for more than ten years he drank no wine and ate no meat.

value.zh: 親族迭謂之曰：「少孤！
value.en: Kinsmen pleaded, "Shaogu!
value.literal: Lineage kin in turn said to him, "Shaogu!

value.zh: 誰無父母？
value.en: Who has no parents?
value.literal: Who lacks parents?

value.zh: 誰有父母！
value.en: Who keeps parents forever?
value.literal: Who has parents!

value.zh: 聖人制禮，令賢者俯就，不肖企及。
value.en: The sages set rites so the wise may ease grief and fools may aim higher.
value.literal: The sages fixed ritual to let the worthy bend down and the unworthy strive up.

value.zh: 若使毀性無嗣，更為不孝也。」
value.en: To die childless is the greater unfilial act."
value.literal: If you destroy your nature and leave no heir, that is again unfilial.

value.zh: 陋感此言，然後從吉。
value.en: He heard them, relented, and ended mourning properly.
value.literal: Lou was moved by these words; then afterward he followed auspicious rites.

value.zh: 由是名著海內。
value.en: His name then filled the empire.
value.literal: From this his name was famed within the seas.

value.zh: 簡文帝輔政，命為參軍，稱疾不起。
value.en: Emperor Jianwen summoned him as adviser; he pleaded illness.
value.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he ordered him as adviser; he claimed illness and did not rise.

value.zh: 桓溫躬往造焉。
value.en: Huan Wen himself knocked on his door.
value.literal: Huan Wen in person went to visit him.

value.zh: 或謂溫曰：「孟陋高行，學為儒宗，宜引在府，以和鼎味。」
value.en: A friend told Huan Wen, 'Meng Lou's virtue tops the scholars; bring him to your staff to leaven the court.'
value.literal: Someone said to Wen, "Meng Lou's conduct is lofty; his learning is patriarch of Confucians—it is fitting to draw him into the office to harmonize the cauldron's flavor."

value.zh: 溫歎曰：「會稽王尚不能屈，非敢擬議也。」
value.en: Wen sighed, 'Even the prince of Kuaiji could not move him—I hardly dare speak of hiring him.'
value.literal: Wen sighed, saying, "The prince of Kuaiji still could not bend him—how dare I presume to discuss it."

value.zh: 陋聞之曰：「桓公正當以我不往故耳。
value.en: Lou heard and said, 'Huan Wen only thinks I snubbed him on purpose.
value.literal: Lou heard it and said, "Lord Huan only thinks it is because I did not go.

value.zh: 億兆之人，無官者十居其九，豈皆高士哉！
value.en: Nine men in ten lack office—are they all recluses?
value.literal: Of the myriad million men, nine in ten have no office—are they all lofty gentlemen!

value.zh: 我疾病不堪恭相王之命，非敢為高也。」
value.en: I am too sick to obey the prince's summons—that is no pose of pride.'
value.literal: I am ill and cannot bear the respectful commands of the minister king—it is not that I dare be lofty."

value.zh: 由是名稱益重。
value.en: His name only grew weightier after that.
value.literal: From this his reputation and title grew heavier.

value.zh: 博學多通，長於《三禮》。
value.en: He mastered the Three Rites.
value.literal: He was broadly learned and penetrating, excelling in the Three Rites.

value.zh: 注《論語》，行於世。
value.en: His Analects commentary circulates still.
value.literal: He annotated the Analects, which circulated in the world.

value.zh: 卒以壽終。
value.en: He died in ripe old age.
value.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.

value.zh: 劉元海（子和） 劉宣
value.en: Liu Yuanhai (with his son He) and Liu Xuan.
value.literal: Liu Yuanhai (son: He) and Liu Xuan.

value.en: (His son He)
value.literal: (Son: He)

value.zh: 劉宣
value.en: Liu Xuan.
value.literal: Liu Xuan.

value.zh: 東嬴公騰使將軍聶玄討之，戰於大陵，玄師敗績，騰懼，率并州二萬餘戶下山東，遂所在為寇。
value.en: Sima Teng sent Nie Xuan against him, lost at Daling, then fled Bing with twenty thousand families eastward, leaving the province to chaos.
value.literal: Dongying Duke Teng sent General Nie Xuan to attack him; they fought at Daling; Xuan's army was routed; Teng, in fear, led more than twenty thousand households of Bingzhou down to Shandong, and thereupon everywhere became bandits.

value.zh: 元海遣其建武將軍劉曜寇太原、泫氏、屯留、長子、中都，皆陷之。
value.en: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao to storm Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.
value.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Establishes Might Liu Yao to raid Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.

value.zh: 二年，騰又遣司馬瑜、周良、石鮮等討之，次於離石汾城。
value.en: Next year Sima Teng sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, and Shi Xian to Lishi's Fencheng.
value.literal: In the second year Teng again sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, Shi Xian, and others to attack him, halting at Fencheng of Lishi.

value.zh: 元海遣其武牙將軍劉欽等六軍距瑜等，四戰，瑜皆敗，欽振旅而歸。
value.en: Liu Yuan sent Liu Qin with six hosts; after four battles Jin fled and Liu Qin marched home in triumph.
value.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Martial Fangs Liu Qin and six armies to oppose Yu and the others; after four battles Yu was defeated each time, and Qin returned with drums beating.

value.zh: 是歲，離石大饑，遷于黎亭，以就邸閣穀，留其太尉劉宏、護軍馬景守離石，使大司農卜豫運糧以給之。
value.en: Famine struck Lishi, so the court moved to Liting granaries while Liu Hong and Ma Jing held Lishi and Bu Yu shipped grain.
value.literal: That year Lishi suffered great famine; they moved to Liting to draw on granary grain, leaving Grand Commandant Liu Hong and Protector Ma Jing to guard Lishi, and ordered Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain to supply them.

value.zh: 以其前將軍劉景為使持節、征討大都督、大將軍，要擊并州刺史劉琨于版橋，為琨所敗，琨遂據晉陽。
value.en: He sent Liu Jing to ambush Liu Kun at Banqiao; Liu Kun crushed him and took Jinyang.
value.literal: He made his former general Liu Jing credential-holder, grand commander for conquest, grand general, and intercepted Bing Governor Liu Kun at Banqiao; he was defeated by Kun, and Kun thereupon occupied Jinyang.

value.zh: 其侍中劉殷、王育進諫元海曰：「殿下自起兵以來，漸已一周，而顓守偏方，王威未震。
value.en: Liu Yin and Wang Yu urged him: "A year has passed and you still hug one corner—your majesty has not yet thundered abroad.
value.literal: His attendants Liu Yin and Wang Yu advanced remonstrance to Yuanhai, saying, "Since Your Highness raised troops it has gradually been a full cycle, yet you only hold a corner; kingly awe has not yet shaken.

value.zh: 誠能命將四出，決機一擲，梟劉琨，定河東，建帝號，鼓行而南，克長安而都之，以關中之眾席捲洛陽，如指掌耳。
value.en: Send four columns, kill Liu Kun, secure Hedong, proclaim the throne, march on Chang'an, then sweep from the passes to Luoyang like turning your hand.
value.literal: If you truly can order generals to go out on four sides, cast the die once, behead Liu Kun, settle Hedong, establish an imperial title, beat the drum southward, take Chang'an as capital, then with the hosts of Guanzhong roll up Luoyang—it is like turning the palm.

value.zh: 此高皇帝之所以創啟鴻基，克殄強楚者也。」
value.en: That was Gaozu's road to crush Chu."
value.literal: This is how the High Emperor opened the great foundation and utterly destroyed mighty Chu."

value.zh: 元海悅曰：「此孤心也。」
value.en: Liu Yuan cried, "That is my own mind too."
value.literal: Yuanhai, pleased, said, "This is Our heart."

value.zh: 遂進據河東，攻寇蒲阪、平陽，皆陷之。
value.en: He drove into Hedong, stormed Puyin and Pingyang, and took both.
value.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Hedong, attacked and raided Puyin and Pingyang, and both fell.

value.zh: 元海遂入都蒲子，河東、平陽屬縣壘壁盡降。
value.en: He moved the capital to Puzi; every fort in Hedong and Pingyang opened its gates.
value.literal: Yuanhai thereupon entered and made his capital at Puzi; fortified camps of the counties of Hedong and Pingyang all surrendered.

value.zh: 時汲桑起兵趙魏，上郡四部鮮卑陸逐延、氏酋大單于征、東萊王彌及石勒等並相次降之，元海悉署其官爵，
value.en: Ji Sang rose in Zhao-Wei; Xianbei, Di, Wang Mi, and Shi Le came over in turn; Liu Yuan handed each a title.
value.literal: At that time Ji Sang raised troops in Zhao and Wei; Lüzhuyan of the four Xianbei sections of Shangjun, Di chief Great-Shanyu Zheng, Wang Mi of Donglai, and Shi Le in succession each surrendered to him; Yuanhai all appointed their offices and noble ranks,

value.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。
value.en: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.
value.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.

value.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。
value.en: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.
value.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.

value.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。
value.en: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.
value.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.

value.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。
value.en: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.
value.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.

value.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。
value.en: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.
value.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.

value.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。
value.en: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.
value.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.

value.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御座，太子獻明皇帝諱寔格之，傷脅。
value.en: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the throne; the crown prince—the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi—blocked him and was wounded in the flank.
value.literal: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the imperial seat; the crown prince, the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi, blocked him and was wounded in the flank.

value.zh: 夏五月，薨，後追諡焉。
value.en: In the fifth month of summer he died; a posthumous title was conferred later.
value.literal: In the fifth month of summer he died; posthumous title was conferred afterward.

value.zh: 秋七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。
value.en: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.

value.zh: 是年，司馬弈臣桓溫，廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。
value.en: That year Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and enthroned Rui's son Yu.
value.literal: That year the minister Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and installed Rui's son Yu.

value.zh: 三十五年，司馬昱死，子昌明僭立。
value.en: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died, and his son Changming usurped the throne.
value.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died; his son Changming usurped the throne.

value.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷
value.en: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83
value.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83

value.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。
value.en: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.
value.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.

value.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；
value.en: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;
value.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;

value.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。
value.en: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.
value.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.

value.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。
value.en: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.
value.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.

value.zh: 允稱疾不拜。
value.en: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.
value.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.

value.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。
value.en: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.
value.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.

value.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。
value.en: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.
value.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.

value.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」
value.en: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
value.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

value.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」
value.en: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."
value.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."

value.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。
value.en: Many rallied to him.
value.literal: At this very many came over to him.

value.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。
value.en: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.
value.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.

value.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。
value.en: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.
value.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.

value.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。
value.en: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.
value.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.

value.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。
value.en: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.
value.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.

value.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。
value.en: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.
value.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.

value.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」
value.en: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
value.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."

value.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。
value.en: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.
value.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.

value.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」
value.en: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."
value.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."

value.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。
value.en: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
value.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

value.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；
value.en: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yin dismounted to receive the edict;
value.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yin dismounted to receive the edict;

value.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。
value.en: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.
value.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.

value.zh: 曲赦洛陽。
value.en: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
value.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

value.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。
value.en: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, whom he had often flogged.
value.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.

value.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。
value.en: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.
value.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.
